name: TPP 92406 6 well
author: Ramona Optics
notes: TPP tissue culture test plate, 6 round flat-bottom wells, clear polystyrene, TC-treated growth surface ('opto-mechanically treated' per TPP, with a flat growth surface intended for imaging), sterile (SAL 10-3, ISO 11137), non-pyrogenic (endotoxins < 0.06 EU/mL), supplied with a lid. Every dimension in this file is read from TPP's controlling datasheet 'TPP Tissue Culture Test Plate - Dimensions and Measurements', document 'TechDoc Test Plates Measurements 04/2026', published at web_reference; pages 3 and 4 of that document define the dimension symbols (X1/Y1 are the A1 well center measured from the left and top edges, P/Q are the horizontal and vertical well-to-well distances, T is the well depth from the top surface to the inner well floor, D is the well top diameter, d the ground diameter, G the bottom thickness and H the plate height without its lid) and pages 5-6 carry the per-format tables. PART NUMBER: the requester's plate is catalogue 92406, which TPP's ordering table lists as the multi-pack presentation (4 plates per bag, 72 per case) of the same 6-well mould as 92006 (1/bag, 126/case) and 92106 (small packaging unit); the 92006 and 92406 rows on https://www.tpp.ch/page/produkte/09_zellkultur_testplatte.php are identical in growth area (9.026 cm^2), internal diameter (33.90 mm), bottom form (F, flat), material and 128 x 86 x 22 mm outer dimensions, differing only in packaging and case weight. The measurements datasheet tabulates the 6-well column under 92006 only, so the geometry here is that column, applied to 92406 on TPP's own statement that the presentations differ in packaging alone; any of the three can use this definition. Distributors write this number 'TP-92406' or 'TP 92406'. Units in meters. Measured values, in millimeters on the datasheet: footprint L = 127.8, B = 85.5; plate height without lid H = 20.2 (22.4 with the lid on, which is the rounded '22' the catalogue rows quote and is not modelled here; tolerance +/-0.1; stack height 19.2 without lid, 21.4 with); skirt R = 8.8. Well pitch P = Q = 37.5 in both directions; grid is 2 rows (A-B) x 3 columns (1-3) with A1 top-left. Well top diameter D = 34.5, recorded in 'diameter' per the top-diameter convention; well ground diameter d = 33.9 (this is the 'internal diameter' TPP quotes in its catalogue, and it is the number that reproduces the stated 9.026 cm^2 growth area: pi x (33.9/2)^2 = 902.6 mm^2). Well depth T = 17.2; flat bottom. The depth and ground diameter cross-check against the stated maximum well volume: pi x (33.9/2)^2 x 17.2 = 15525 mm^3 = 15.52 mL, which is the datasheet's 'max well volume 15.52 mL' to four significant figures. WORKING DISTANCE: bottom thickness G = 1.35 mm in polystyrene - note this is not constant across the TPP family (the 12-well is 1.5 mm and the 96-well 1.2 mm), so it must not be carried over from a sibling format; the well floor sits B = 3.1 mm above the plate ground and C = 1.75 mm above the plate support surface. Recommended media volume 1.8-4.5 mL per well, maximum well volume 15.52 mL. A1 OFFSETS: the datasheet gives X1 = 24.4 and Y1 = 24.0, with last-well centers Xn = 99.5 and Yn = 61.5. Both offsets are used as printed. Vertically the plate is exactly centered - (85.5 - 37.5) / 2 = 24.0 - and Y1 + Q = 61.5 reproduces the tabulated Yn exactly. Horizontally the grid is NOT centered: the centered value would be (127.8 - 2 x 37.5) / 2 = 26.4, so TPP places A1 2.0 mm to the left of center. That is deliberate rather than a typo - the 24-well column in the same table is offset by exactly the same 2.0 mm - but it has not been checked against a plate in hand, and it is the value most worth verifying on the instrument. The table's own Xn is internally inconsistent by 0.1 mm: X1 + 2 x P = 24.4 + 75.0 = 99.4, where the table prints Xn = 99.5. X1 and P are the primary dimensions (X1 = 26.4 - 2.0 exactly, and P = 37.5 is exact against the footprint), and Xn is the derived column, so X1 = 24.4 and P = 37.5 are used and the printed Xn is treated as a rounding artifact. The same 0.1 mm inconsistency does not appear in the 24-, 48- or 96-well columns, which are all self-consistent. Use 'pitch' and origin reference to compute all well centers.
